name: Tangchangya
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: [p.71] Tanchangyas speak a distinctly eastern variety of Indo-Aryan, which despite falling in line with the Southeastern (Chittagong) dialect of Bengali, retains several features of Tibeto-Burman, viz., dentalisation of palatal and palato-alveolar obstruents, aspiration of word initial [t], substitution of [r] by [j] in the environment of the palatal vowel [i], and occurrence of tone contrasts with changes in laryngeal and supra-laryngeal settings of phonemes. [p.79] In Tanchangya, there are several pairs of homophonous words, whose precise meanings are conveyed by the speaker using a two-way tonal contrast. ... But these findings are only preliminary and require extensive study to arrive at definite conclusions.
new_statements.citation: Debnath, Rupak. 2008. Ethnographic Study of Tanchangya of CHT, CADC, Sittwe and South Tripura. Kolkata: Kreativmind.
new_statements.locator: ch. 2, sec. 2.6 'Language', p. 71 (PDF p. 88) and sec. 2.6.2 'Phonology', p. 79 (PDF p. 96)
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accessible phonological sketch reports a (preliminary) two-way lexical tone contrast, low level vs low fall (e.g. za 'go' vs za 'jungle', bisi 'seed' vs bisi 'mongoose'), and gives no statement on the position or existence of word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Author states tone shapes are affected by voice quality and consonant elision (glottal stop from IA h- elided leaving a low-fall tone); flags the tonal analysis as preliminary. Vowel length said to be non-distinctive.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level minimal pairs in citation form; sub-dialects by clan (Karwa, Muo, Daingnya, Melong, Mongla, Langbasa, Angya gosa) noted but tone data not localized to one.
new_statements.identity_note: Debnath 2008 describes Tanchangya as spoken in the CHT (Bangladesh), CADC Mizoram and South Tripura (India), with clan-based sub-dialects (Karwa, Muo, Daingnya, Melong, Mongla, Langbasa, Angya gosa); all fall under tang1330 (no Glottolog sub-dialect codes). The closest described sister language is Chakma (chak1266), for which Huziwara 2019 reports a pitch-accent system; that must not be transferred to Tanchangya without a source.

sources.note: Sec. 2.6.2 Phonology (pp. 74-80) is segmental plus a paragraph on tone: p.71 'occurrence of tone contrasts', p.79 'a two-way tonal contrast' (low level vs low fall; minimal pairs za 'go'/'jungle', bisi 'seed'/'mongoose'), which the author calls preliminary. Nothing at all on stress or accent placement.

sources.citation: Phukan, Satyakam. 2013. An analysis of the ethno-linguistic roots and connections of the Chakma-Tanchangya people. Self-published web PDF.
sources.note: Lexical comparison with Assamese; no prosody.

sources.citation: Tanchangya, Shanta Rakshit. 2013. A comparative analysis of Chakma and English vowels. BA thesis, BRAC University (CORE 61804129).
sources.note: About Chakma, not Tanchangya: reports (after Sugata Chakma) that 'stress at the initial position on the vowels can make different meanings' in Chakma. Sister-language context only.
No grammar, sketch or phonology listed (only Phayre 1841, Bernot, Bessaignet, Loeffler overviews).

sources.citation: Huziwara Keisuke. 2019. Chakma phonology [チャクマ語音韻論]. Journal of Kijutsuken 11: 51-102 (held under../chak1266/).
sources.note: Sister language Chakma only (pitch accent H/L; stress non-distinctive). Grep for Tanchangya/タンチャンギャ in text and bibliography: no mention, cites no Tanchangya description.
